content:
incident-bot: Automated page fired -> high-p95-latency.az3 (threshold crossed: p95 > 1200ms) :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: HIGH - region:az3 latency spike (#PAGER: high-p95-latency-az3)
oncall-alex: acked. I'm oncall for az3, taking lead. Creating incident thread here.
oncall-alex: quick status? impact visible on hosted API, a subset of customers in EU report >1.2s p95 and some timeouts. No full outage yet.
sre-maya: seeing NIC errors and retransmits on several runtime hosts in pool az3-rt-*. kernel logs show repeated rx errors.
sre-maya: logs:
```
2026-03-15T20:12:34Z host=az3-rt-07 kernel: igb 0000:3b:00.0: rx err count 128 -> link flaps
2026-03-15T20:12:36Z host=az3-rt-11 net: TCP retransmit seq 0x9f4 ...
```
eng-runtime-john: taking runtime / model shard perspective. KV cache evictions spiked; some model shards queue depth doubled. Suspect NIC-level packet loss + backpressure in shard queues.
eng-runtime-john: running quick check and will push route weight changes if confirmed.
ops-li: starting routing fallback: will shift traffic away from az3 to az2. Executing weight change now.
ops-li: command:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/weights \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"az3":0,"az2":100}'
```
ops-li: done. controlplane returned 202 Accepted. Waiting for propagation (~30s).
pagerduty-bot: Alert acknowledged by oncall-alex. Escalation paused.
oncall-alex: confirmed traffic shift started. Observability shows az3 traffic dropping, az2 accepting more load. p95 on az3 still high but overall service p95 dropping. :white_check_mark:
sre-maya: I'm SSHing into the suspect host pool and draining nodes with rx errors. Starting rolling kernel module reload and NIC reprobe.
sre-maya: commands run:
```bash
ssh root@az3-rt-07 'systemctl stop inference-runtime && ethtool -r eth0'
kubectl -n infra cordon az3-rt-07 && kubectl -n infra drain az3-rt-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
eng-runtime-john: also executing runtime-level mitigations: increasing per-zone replicas in az2 and bumping KV cache capacity on failover variants.
eng-runtime-john: commands:
```bash
redwoodctl scale --zone az2 --pool infer-runtime --replicas 50
redwoodctl config set --pool infer-runtime --kv-cache-size 1.5x
```
customer-success-anna: posting incident update to status page: "Partial degradation in EU region (az3). Traffic is being routed to alternative zone; some customers may see elevated latency. We're investigating; next update in 15 minutes."
oncall-alex: great. CS notified key customers via direct message as well.
ops-li: propagation looks stable. Rolling failover completed. Metrics: overall p95 dropped from 1400ms -> 420ms after weight change. Error rate reduced ~70%.
sre-maya: NIC errors are decreasing after drain and reprobe on a few hosts. Still monitoring link stats.
oncall-alex: brief runbook check: triggering fallback activation action log entry.
eng-runtime-john: noted a small model-shard hot-spot on az2 due to uneven shard placement. Rebalancing now (non-disruptive).
eng-runtime-john: rebal command:
```bash
redwoodctl rebalance-shards --from-zone az2 --to-zone az2 --max-concurrent 4
```
(oncall-alex reaction) :thumbsup: to eng/runtime and sre.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note - escalation policy suppressed while oncall handling.
oncall-alex: starting handoff to maya for deeper recovery and post-incident timeline. I'll remain reachable for questions.
noncall-alex: ETA for postmortem draft 2hrs, public status updated in 30m.
sre-maya: taking over. will monitor until link errors fully clear and confirm safe return-to-service for az3.
ops-li: plan to slowly shift a small percentage back after we see clean link stats for 10m: will test with canary weight: az3=10 az2=90.
sre-maya: canary started. no error spikes on bring-back.
customer-success-anna: updated customers: "We've routed traffic away from the affected AZ and are verifying full recovery; minimal customer impact expected going forward."
incident-bot: Page resolved -> high-p95-latency.az3 (auto-resolve by controlplane) :white_check_mark:
oncall-alex: closing thread for now. Handoff complete to maya for post-incident cleanup and RCA.
sre-maya: noted follow-ups: (1) investigate root NIC failure pattern on host family 3b:00, (2) improve automated canary weights to avoid double-shift oscillation, (3) add runbook step to check kernel RX counters earlier.
oncall-alex: thanks all.
customer-success-anna: will send final customer comms after RCA.
